[43030 Professional Practice in Computing | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject focuses on tools and techniques used in the professional practice of design, implementation, cybersecurity, and maintenance of computing systems and related software systems. You will gain an understanding of professional standards, codes of conduct, and methodologies for ensuring high quality outcomes in the various domains within which computing systems are employed and how to convey professional progression in these areas.

[43030 Professional Practice in Computing | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject uses a combination of self-paced online content and industry relevant examples, activities and assessment. 
The subject encourages students to reflect on their learning and professional development goals. Uses this as a scaffold, the subject allows students to access learning relevant to these goals, develop a portfolio that demonstrates their progression and supports them in reflecting upon this progression, alongside direct development of professionally relevant skills and knowledge.
The assessment tasks support this development, guiding students through the process of analysing their own professional needs and how to select goals from feasible options to meet these needs. It further supports developing professional communication of their progression and achievement.

title: Learning outcomes

[43030 Professional Practice in Computing | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Critically reflect on ethical principles of stakeholder engagement to work effectively with and for Indigenous Australians across the IT profession. (A.1)
SLO2: Synthesise the priorities and goals of a professional required to work in industry. (B.1)
SLO3: Provide evidence of professionally relevant technical skills and knowledge that contribute to improved professional practice. (D.1)
SLO4: Justify your professional development toward a professional pathway. (E.1)
SLO5: Describe approaches taken to ensure future projects are aligned to Industry ethical practices. (F.1)
